column1: # Every project in the Gamespice family, and where it is cloned from.
# THIS IS THE ONLY COPY OF THIS LIST. bootstrap.sh and bootstrap.ps1 both read
# it, and `bootstrap --check` fails if a repository on disk is missing from it
# or a line here names something that is not there. Two copies of one list is
# the bug the list was guarding against, and this family has shipped that bug
# three times already: setup.sh against tools/check.sh against
# tools/package_check.sh, and bootstrap's own manifest, which had drifted to 19
# of 33 projects and had silently lost two of the five games.
# The addons each project needs are NOT here on purpose. They are derived from
# the /addons/<name> lines in that project's own .gitignore, which is the one
# place that can be right: the repository that gains a dependency is the
# repository that has to ignore its link, so the list maintains itself.
# This repository is not listed. It is the thing doing the cloning.
# Columns: name <TAB> clone URL, or the word LOCAL for a project with no remote
# yet -- a LOCAL project cannot be cloned onto another machine at all. An
# optional third column lists other names for it, comma-separated, which every
# selection, --play and --export accept. A renamed repository is listed, and
# cloned, under its NEW name, and its old names go in this column:
# game-fatal-contact answers to its old FC names. The next sync moves a
# checkout still under an old name to the new one (only a clean move: never over
# an existing folder, never while a process works in it) and leaves a link at
# the old name; games' .gitignore lines that still say the legacy /addons/arena_weapons or
# "# bootstrap-link: g2gfast-maps/maps" resolve through this column. fc-weapons
# holds addons/fc_weapons; a game whose .gitignore still names the legacy
# /addons/arena_weapons is linked to it (with a deprecation warning) only while the
# fc-weapons checkout still holds that directory, and is an error once it does not.
# A checkout whose origin still names the old repository is repointed at the
# URL here on the next sync (GitHub's redirect for a renamed repository is not
# something to lean on: it ends the moment a repository takes the old name).
# TWO OWNERS, and the split is a rule rather than a set of accidents: the official
# addons are the organisation's (`gamespice-platform/*`, the dot- prefix dropped) and the games, and any addon
# that is the author's own (dot-radio), are theirs (`zees-games/`). That is why the URL is written out per line here instead of being
# derived from the name -- the name says what a project IS, not who owns it, and a
# derivation would have to encode the split in two places. setup.sh's repo_url()
# encodes the same rule for the one case that cannot read this file: a fresh box
# cloning the sources it needs before dot-bootstrap is on it.
# A project named game-* has a playable client: `bootstrap --play <name>`.
